stumbles.quote: The two judges labelled 58 of those 63 as legitimate prose, because table cells hold numbers and labels rather than sentences.
stumbles.why: "The two judges" are never introduced (humans? models?). The sentence also contradicts itself: it says the cells were labelled "legitimate prose", but the reason given is that table cells are not prose. The intended meaning is probably that the hits were false positives.

stumbles.quote: 63 of its 300 hits were inside Markdown table cells.
stumbles.why: Only 58 of 63 (about 19% of all hits) were judged false positives. It is unclear why that justifies a flag, and the 5 remaining hits are not discussed.

stumbles.quote: `--skip-quoted` already blanks table cells, along with blockquotes and italics.
stumbles.why: This makes the new flag look redundant. The justification only appears in the next sentence. It also conflicts with the claim that `--skip-tables` "still scans everything else", unless you already know the flags differ in scope.
"declaude_lint.py" and the "declauding" skill are never explained. You can't tell what a "hit" is or what "legitimate prose" means as a lint result.

point: The PR adds a `--skip-tables` flag to the declauding linter that blanks lines starting with `|` (keeping line numbers) so table cells stop producing false positives, and unlike `--skip-quoted` it still lints italics and blockquotes.
